cells.tense: Right now you can see the pattern and keep walking at the same time.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Something already has your weight behind it, and nothing on the calendar is forcing it. Stay with the tug before you settle what it is. Then keep moving the way you were moving.
cells.core:
You can read the shape of a thing while it is still being built, and keep walking at the same time. That is rarer than it sounds. The pattern shows up early for you, and instead of stopping to admire it, you fold it into the next step and keep your weight going forward. At your best, the reading and the walking are the same motion. You notice what is actually there, and it feeds the direction instead of replacing it.

Something is drawing you right now — you know which one. Let it stay a tug before you turn it into anything. No choosing, no announcing, no plan. Watch what it does to the way you move. Some of the momentum you carry will want to close the question early; that is the habit, not the destination. Staying open costs a little speed and buys a truer aim.
cells.sheetLine: You can read the pattern and keep walking at once.
cells.verb: reading the shape of a thing before it is finished being built
cells.place: on the road toward something with your whole weight forward

cells.tense: Soon you will be bracing for a version of this that has not happened yet.
cells.act: let the structure act instead of announcing it
cells.ask: Once you have decided something, skip the explanation — no reasoning, no plan walked through. Carry the decision and watch what happens without the case to back it.
cells.core:
Your mind is fast and it sees what is coming. Lately it has been running the future at full volume, and your legs are already halfway there — braced for a version of the thing that has not happened. The pattern is right; the timing is off. You are solving three moves out and standing in a future you cannot walk in yet, and the walking part, the part happening today, gets the leftovers. Nothing about the destination is wrong. You are just arriving before the road.

Part of this is the explaining. When you have decided something, you reach for the case to make it land correctly, and the case is a kind of bracing. Try it differently once. Make your call and carry it, and say nothing about the why. Some people will misread it, and you will want to correct them. Sit with that instead. The structure works without the announcement, and you find out what your decisions look like when they are not being defended.
cells.sheetLine: You are solving a future you cannot walk in yet.

cells.tense: You were on a road, and you have been standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: leave the hollow ritual for the living one
cells.ask: A habit has been running past its meaning. Let it go by without you, and put that hour toward someone you would be glad to see — a call, a meal, nothing ceremonial.
cells.core:
You used to have direction. The reading of patterns is still running, but it sits in the mind now instead of moving the legs. There is a road you were on, and you have been standing at a door that is already behind you — turning toward it, tending it, not walking. Something you do keeps happening, and it stopped connecting to anything a while back. The drive is not broken. It is pointed at an older version of the question.

More effort on the goal will not do it. Something living will. Let one practice or obligation go by without you, the one that stopped being true. Give that hour to a person you would actually be glad to see — no ceremony, no fixing, just the visit. What you are looking for is a place where the connection is real enough to pull you forward again. That pull is what your direction runs on. You will know it when it moves you, because you will not have to talk yourself into the next step.
cells.sheetLine: You tend a door that is already behind you.

cells.place: on the road toward something with your whole weight forward

cells.tense: You are moving, and you would tell anyone that the direction arranged itself.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: A pull has been drawing you quietly and has no good reason yet. Go toward it once. Keep nothing after — no plan, no decision, no account of why.
cells.core:
You are moving well, and you would tell anyone the direction arranged itself. Work, choices, the next step — they happen, and they look to you like circumstance or someone else's plan you are simply carrying through. Some of that is true. But ask anyone who has watched you closely and they will tell you the call was yours, the reading was yours, the work was yours. That part is real. What is missing is your name on it, and you have been leaving that credit on the table for a while.

There is a pull you have been keeping off the books — something that draws you a little and has no good reason yet. Go toward it once, and stop there. No decision, no plan, nothing written down after. It will feel smaller than you expect, and it will have been yours. You do not need to justify the move to anyone, including the voice that says it was nothing special.
cells.sheetLine: The direction was yours. It just went unsigned.
cells.verb: reading the shape of a thing before it is finished being built
cells.place: on the road toward something with your whole weight forward

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person experiences drive as momentum toward destinations they can name; many people with this signature move hard toward goals they would not call theirs if asked. A reader could reasonably say the direction is not theirs, or that the analysis is the tired part, not the motion. The asks survive a wrong read because each one is small, finishable, and teaches something about where their attention actually goes even if the diagnosis is off. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is the 'seeing patterns that liberate' line in Too Much, which flatters the card at the person's expense; it is cut from the glass.
